blind.description: A stylised, hand-painted medieval wooden hoist or mine headframe structure. It consists of four thick timber upright legs splayed outward and joined by horizontal crossbeams, reinforced at joints with dark iron bands and brackets. At the top rests an axle supporting a large wooden pulley wheel wrapped with a thick coiled rope that hangs down into the open center. All surfaces are clean, solid, and continuous with no disconnected or floating parts.
blind.from_above: A rectangular timber framework enclosing a central wooden pulley wheel with rope wrapped over it, metal corner brackets, and open ground visible through the framing below.
blind.height_vs_figure: About 1.3 to 1.4 times the height of the 5 ft 9 in figure (approximately 7.5 to 8 feet tall), with a ground footprint about 4.5 to 5 feet wide.
